results.references: - Yu. E. Nesterov. [A method of solving a convex programming problem with convergence rate O(1/k²)](https://hengshuaiyao.github.io/papers/nesterov83.pdf). 1983. Complexity: $O(1+\sqrt{LR^2/\varepsilon})$ exact-gradient calls using the known-$L$ accelerated gradient method, with no function-value calls, for deterministic objective gap at most $\varepsilon$ (hence also expected gap).

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained convex minimization of a globally differentiable function with L-Lipschitz gradient; a global minimizer lies within distance R of x0.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Each call returns the exact gradient at the queried point for every history and oracle seed. Gradient uniqueness excludes oracle noise despite the general randomized oracle interface.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SmoothAndConvex.lean: spec.admissible, HasGradientAt condition; LongTails/Template.lean: Oracle.answer.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: Euclidean space R^d. All parameters d,L,x0,R,ε are public. Validity requires L,R,ε>0, 262144ε≤LR², and 65536(floor(sqrt(LR²/ε)/512)+1)^5≤d.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: Output a point whose objective gap relative to a global minimizer is integrable and at most ε in expectation.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: Expectation is over the product of algorithm and oracle seed laws; no almost-sure accuracy is required.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: Standard smooth convex exact-gradient minimization with an expected objective-gap target; the additional dimension and accuracy restrictions select a benchmark parameter regime.
